findingsFromCp2.causeHunt: The counting rule is NOT the explanation, which was the first hypothesis and was checked rather than assumed: DISTINCT ON (feature_index) could in principle pick an unstamped duplicate row for a feature that is stamped on another row. findingsFromCp2.label: VERIFIED by SS-W12
findingsFromCp2.finding: The existing CI gate 'ci-coverage-clamp' greps for the clamp in exactly two named files (countyGeometryScoreCli.ts, countyCoverageScoreCli.ts). It guards the FILES the defect was found in, not the RULE. A clamp introduced in the new shared engine would reach all 14 rails at once with the gate still green.
findingsFromCp2.disposition: FIXED in this PR: a new step scopes the SF-25 rule to artifacts/api-server/src/lib/railScoring.
twoDefectsInTheGateItself: The first draft of the new grep was PERMANENTLY RED, because the engine's own header quotes 'Math.min(100, (n/feat)*100)' while documenting the defect it prevents. A gate nobody can get to green is a dead gate (DEV_PROCESS 2.0) and this is CTRL-3 mirrored: there, a defect report's prose granted a bad row authority. Comment lines are now excluded and the grep matches CODE.

The second draft was FAIL-OPEN: the whole pipeline was wrapped in '|| true', so when ripgrep was not on PATH the gate printed 'clean' and exited 0. Caught by running it, not by reading it. The exit code is now taken from rg itself, never from the pipe (DEV_PROCESS 2.3), and >1 is a hard failure.
findingsFromCp2.provenAbleToFire: both predicates exercised on real exit codes: rg exit 0 and 1 proceed, 2 and 127 fail the gate; the line filter drops 4 comment forms (leading *, //, /*, and a doc line) and keeps the 1 real code line

findingsFromCp2.label: VERIFIED by SS-W12

findingsFromCp2.label: VERIFIED by SS-W12
findingsFromCp2.finding: The parcel-feature denominator was being re-measured once per (rail, county) rather than once per county: a 14-rail statewide run would have issued 14 count(DISTINCT feature_index) scans per county for one unchanging number. The per-rail-CLI pattern paid this cost invisibly because each CLI only knew about its own rail.
findingsFromCp2.disposition: FIXED in this PR: memoised per run, never at module level, so a run always sees the store as it is now.

adversarialReviewAtCp2.challenge: The dry run reported 41 of 42 cells changed. Does that mean the harness disagrees with the ledger almost everywhere?
adversarialReviewAtCp2.answer: No, and the fact that the question is askable was itself the defect (F7). 16 cells moved on coverage; 25 changed only their provenance strings. Of the 16: 6 are cells with no prior row at all, 4 are the geometry accounted-vs-raw denominator difference (state unchanged), 2 are the cad clamp, 2 are zoning, 2 are envelope legacy rows. landuse and owner moved zero of twelve.

adversarialReviewAtCp2.challenge: You claim the capability reproduces existing scorers, but you tested 6 counties out of 254.
adversarialReviewAtCp2.answer: Stated with its denominator rather than generalized. The claim is: on 6 counties x 7 rails, flood reproduced 4 of 4 stored values exactly and landuse/owner reproduced 12 of 12 exactly. It is NOT a statewide equivalence claim and the close does not make one. A statewide dry run is cheap to add and is named as the precondition for any apply.

adversarialReviewAtCp2.challenge: Preserving absences by default could hide a genuinely stale absence forever.
adversarialReviewAtCp2.answer: It could, and that is the deliberate trade. The asymmetry: a wrongly-preserved absence is visible in the report on every single run (absencesPreserved), while a wrongly-destroyed absence is invisible and unrecoverable. The escape hatch exists and is one flag, and a test proves the guard releases rather than being stuck closed.

adversarialReviewAtCp2.challenge: The route cannot score atom-count rails in production and you shipped it anyway.
adversarialReviewAtCp2.answer: It fails closed and NAMED (railsUnavailable / atoms_store_not_configured), with a test asserting zero writes on that path. The gap is now readable from the route's own response instead of being invisible. Wiring ATOMS_DATABASE_URL onto the service is a planner deploy decision and is listed in the close, not done here.
